edges.reason: Plethori constructor reads tx.origin to derive privileged state and allowances.
owner is assigned from tx.origin, allowing a phishing contract to become owner.
msg.sender is used both as allowance spender and as _from in Plethori.transferFrom.
msg.sender == owner gate in delegate; combined with tx.origin ownership this is spoofable.
msg.sender == owner gate in list(), the privileged liquidity and balance overwrite path.
msg.sender becomes the _from argument forwarded by transfer to transferFrom.
approve keys the allowance mapping on msg.sender.
ERC20.transferFrom uses msg.sender as spender for the allowance decrement.
block.timestamp + 600 is used as the router deadline, making execution timestamp dependent.
_value drives the unchecked allowance and balance subtractions and additions in transferFrom.
balanceOf entries are mutated with unchecked -= and += under Solidity 0.7.
allowance entries are mutated with unchecked -= without SafeMath.
_from is caller supplied and bypasses the msg.sender allowance path only when equal to msg.sender.
protectionFromBots address is the target of the low-level call in the modifier.
protectionFromBots address is the target of the low-level call in list().
User supplied address a is used as the delegatecall target.
User supplied bytes b is used as raw delegatecall payload.
_tos is ABI encoded into the unchecked external call made by list().
_amounts are written directly into balanceOf entries without validation.
Plethori.delegate executes the delegatecall to an arbitrary target.
The checkBots modifier performs the low-level protection call before the function body.
checkBots modifier wraps Plethori.transferFrom, executing an external call before state updates.
Plethori.transfer delegates to transferFrom.
Constructor calls pairOfTokens to derive uniPair.
list() invokes routerForPancake.addLiquidityETH with value.
list() performs unconditional balance overwrite of owner and recipient balances.
list() writes privileged values into the balanceOf mapping.
The external protection call runs before transferFrom mutates balances, so a malicious protection contract can re-enter with stale state.
Unchecked external call at the end of list() allows re-entering list() and rewriting balances.
External call to the router while list() is mid-execution creates a reentrancy window.
delegatecall executes attacker code with this contract's storage, allowing owner/storage takeover.
Caller supplied data reaches the delegatecall payload through delegate.
Constructor also sets allowance[tx.origin][uniPair] to uint(-1) based on the origin.
